questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.**

He lost all his hardly earned money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1 i.e. hardly earned money.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **'Hardly'** is an adverb, **which means scarcely.**
 
• **'Hardly earned'** means **'earned not enough', which is incorrect.**
 
• The correct word to use is the adjective 'hard-earned which means 'earned or achieved after a lot of effort'.

**Correct sentence-** *He lost all his **hard-earned **money.*

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1. **
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3 i.e. for.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct preposition to be used in the blank is 'for'.
 
• **For** is used to indicate the reason -- for the school community.
 
• Other options are cancelled as:
 
 
• **On** is used with specific days of the week or year - on 1st of Jan / on Monday.
 
• **At **is used with specific times of the day/ with specific places in a city - at school / at 12 o’clock.
 
• **To** is used with verbs to show movement such as go and come - to school.
 
 

**Hence the sentence is:** *The ﬁrst television programmes were meant** for** schools and rural areas.*

questions.solution:

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

A study suggests that** **__woman is good__ at handling emotions than men.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2 i.e. women are better.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The verb 'suggests' is plural. The object 'men' is plural.
 
• The noun 'emotions' is plural. Hence the first half of the sentence also needs to be in the plural-- 'women are'.
 
• A comparison is being made between women and men so the adverb should be 'better' as it has 'than' following it.

**The sentence should be-** *A study suggests that women are better at handling emotions than men.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.**

They were astonished ______ his failure in the competition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2 i.e. at.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **‘At’** is used to show the cause of something, especially a feeling - at the news.
 
• The given sentence is about the feeling of astonishment, so the right word is 'at'.
 
• The other options are incorrect because-
 
 
• **‘On’** is used with specific days of the week or year - on 1st of Jan / on Monday.
 
• **'From'** is used to show the origin of something or someone - from Mumbai.
 
• **‘In’** is used with months of the year/seasons/countries - in April / in Summer.
 
 

***Correct sentence-** They were astonished **at** his failure in the competition.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.**

He ______ for a week when his father came.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1 i.e. had been ill.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• *The given sentence indicates the past perfect tense as an action that started in the past (for a week) which is shown to have continued up to a given time in the past[father came].*
 
• The form is had been + past participle.

**So the correct sentence is -*** He **had been ill** for a week when his father came.*
